haiku-low.q1: They see the generic 200 message, "If an account exists for that address, we've sent a link." Nothing is written and nothing is sent.
haiku-low.q2: The request is refused: the count of rows from the last 60 minutes is already 3 or more. Nothing is written or sent, and the same generic message is shown.
haiku-low.q3: A link works for 30 minutes after creation (expires_at). It ends sooner when used (used_at set by a successful reset) or when a newer link is issued for the account.
haiku-low.q4: Nothing is written, so the link is still live and keeps working until its expires_at.
haiku-low.q5: None. All the user's sessions are deleted, including the device that did the reset. The user is redirected to /login and logs in with the new password.
haiku-low.q6: It retries the send up to 3 times with backoff, then logs the error and drops the job. The user is not told and must request a new reset.
haiku-low.q7: The raw token is generated in API memory, placed in the queued email job, and included in the emailed link. Only its SHA-256 hash is stored in Postgres.
haiku-low.q8: It hashes the raw token with SHA-256 and looks up reset_tokens by token_hash. The link is OK only if the row exists, used_at is NULL, and expires_at is later than now.
haiku-low.q9: In the reset_tokens table in Postgres. The count is of that account's rows created in the last 60 minutes, so old rows age out by time.
haiku-low.q10: In the same issuing transaction, before inserting the new row, it sets used_at = now on all of the account's unused earlier links, so they die.
haiku-low.q11: In one transaction: mark the token used, update the password hash, and delete all the user's sessions. The password-changed email is queued only after COMMIT.
haiku-low.q12: The token is consumed by a conditional UPDATE (used_at IS NULL and not expired). Only one submit updates a row; the other updates 0 rows, rolls back, and gets the expired-link page.

sonnet.q1: They see the same 200 message as everyone: "If an account exists for that address, we've sent a link." Nothing is written and nothing is sent.
sonnet.q2: The transaction rolls back (count of rows in the last 60 min is >= 3). Nothing is written or sent, and the user gets the same 200 generic message.
sonnet.q3: 30 minutes from creation (expires_at). It ends sooner if used_at is set: by a successful reset, or by a newer link being issued for that account, which kills all earlier unused links.
sonnet.q4: Unchanged and still live. Nothing is written, the form is shown again with the error, and the same link keeps working until its expires_at.
sonnet.q5: None. All session rows for the user are deleted, including the device doing the reset. No session is created; the user is redirected to /login and logs in with the new password.
sonnet.q6: The worker retries with backoff up to 3 retries, then logs an error and drops the job. No one is told; the user has to request again.
sonnet.q7: The raw token is generated in API memory (32 random bytes) at request time, put into the link in the queued email job, and the worker sends that job in the email. The raw token is never stored in Postgres.
sonnet.q8: It looks up reset_tokens by token_hash = SHA-256(raw token from the URL). The link is good only if the row exists, used_at IS NULL, and expires_at > now. row.user_id gives the account.
sonnet.q9: There is no separate counter. It is the count of the account's reset_tokens rows with created_at in the last 60 minutes (live and dead rows both count). Old requests age out when their created_at passes 60 minutes.
sonnet.q10: Within the issuing transaction, after the rate-limit check passes and the raw token is generated and before the new row is inserted, all of the account's earlier unused links are marked used_at = now (not deleted).
sonnet.q11: In one transaction: mark the token used (used_at), update the user's password_hash, and delete all of the user's sessions. The password-changed email job is queued only after COMMIT.
sonnet.q12: In the transaction, the UPDATE sets used_at only WHERE id = row AND used_at IS NULL AND expires_at > now(). Only the first submission updates a row; the other gets 0 rows, rolls back and sees the expired-link page.
